paper.title: Transformer-generated atomic embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy of crystal properties with machine learning
paper.research_summary: This paper proposes a universal atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) generated by a home-made CrystalTransformer model, which learns unique 'fingerprints' for each atom capturing their roles and interactions within materials. The embeddings (ct-UAEs) are pre-trained on large crystal databases (MP*) for formation energy and bandgap prediction, then transferred to various back-end models (CGCNN, MEGNET, ALIGNN) to improve prediction accuracy across multiple datasets (MP, JARVIS, MC3D, hybrid perovskites). The work demonstrates improved MAE (e.g., 14% reduction for formation energy in CGCNN), transferability across tasks and databases, interpretability via clustering (UMAP/K-means revealing periodic-table-aligned groupings), and applicability to data-scarce domains like hybrid perovskites (34% MAE boost in MEGNET).

tasks.task_name_raw: Generate universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) for crystal property prediction
tasks.objective: To generate universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) that serve as broadly applicable atomic fingerprints capable of enhancing the prediction accuracy of crystal properties (e.g., formation energy, bandgap) across diverse deep learning models and material databases.
constraints: must be transferable across different back-end models (CGCNN, MEGNET, ALIGNN)
must be invariant to rotational and translational symmetry
must capture complex atomic features without relying on predefined atomic attributes
output_goal: dense, low-dimensional tensor representations (embeddings) for each atom in a crystal, forming a universal atomic embedding (UAE) tensor

evidence.text: Here, we proposed an atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) for their broad applicability as atomic ﬁngerprints, and generated the UAE tensors based on the proposed CrystalTransformer model.

We developed the home-made CrystalTransformer model to generate universal atomic embeddings called ct-UAEs based on transformer architecture, which learns a unique “ﬁngerprint” for each atom, capturing the essence of their roles and interactions within the materials.
To construct universal atomic embeddings, the vanilla transformer algorithm is introduced as the main part of the model, resulting in the home-made model named CrystalTransformer

stages.stage_goal: Obtain large-scale, high-quality crystal structure and property datasets for training and evaluation.

evidence.text: To examine the atomic embeddings tensors obtained from different models, we used MP and MP* dataset for formation energy (Ef) and PBE bandgap (Eg), which are key properties for evaluating their chemical stabilities and electronic performances. MP stands for the 2018.6.1 version for MP44 dataset, which contains 69,239 materials with properties. MP* denotes the 2023.6.23 version, which contains 134,243 materials.

The ability and transferability of the universal atomic embedding are further tested on different databases and tasks. Each is cut into 8:1:1 for training, validation, and testing. Details on the dataset can be found in Supplementary 2A. As for the Jarvis dataset49, the result is shown in Table 1.

After merging two distinct datasets of HOIP materials69,70, we created a more diverse dataset containing 2103 HOIP crystals, which is still small compared to other material databases such as the MP dataset44.

stages.stage_goal: Prepare raw crystal data for input into the CrystalTransformer model, including topological augmentation and feature transformation.
stage_output: linearly transformed atom and coordinate features

evidence.text: When given an atom input in a batch of size batch for N-atom with L features per atom (L denotes a one-hot encoding of the atomic species) and the coordinate input with batch × N × D size (Here D indicates the spatial dimension (equals 3 in this context)), the model first topologically augments the coordinates input using translation and rotation transformation.

A0 = AW A + bA,
X0 = XW X + bX,
where A denotes the one-hot initialization for atom input features, with the dimension of batch × N × L. Tensor X denotes the atom position coordinates, with the dimension of batch × N × D.

stages.stage_goal: Train the CrystalTransformer model on large crystal databases to learn universal atomic embeddings (ct-UAEs) for target properties.
stage_input: target properties (formation energy, bandgap, total energy, total magnetization)

evidence.text: Front-end models as CrystalTransformer, CGCNN, ALIGNN, and MEGNET are ﬁrst pre-trained on the expanded MP* dataset, focusing on the bandgap energy Eg and formation energy Ef predictive tasks.

MTL72–74 (multi-task learning) is a learning method. The model is trained simultaneously on different tasks, while the parameter is optimized toward the trend that all tasks improve... In the context of CrystalTransformer, MTL stands for different properties for materials.
The CrystalTransformer method exhibits a theoretical complexity primarily driven by the self-attention mechanism in its Transformer layers.

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluate ct-UAE transfer performance on back-end models
stages.stage_goal: Assess the improvement in prediction accuracy when ct-UAEs are integrated into various back-end deep learning models (CGCNN, MEGNET, ALIGNN) across multiple datasets and properties.
stage_output: MAE and R2 scores for formation energy, bandgap, total energy

evidence.text: By performing experiments on widely-used materials database, our CrystalTransformer-based UAEs (ct-UAEs) are shown to accurately capture complex atomic features, leading to a 14% improvement in prediction accuracy on CGCNN and 18% on ALIGNN when using formation energies as the target, based on the Materials Project database.
Table 1 shows a comparative MAE analysis to evaluate the relative performance enhancements attributable to the front-end atomic embeddings...

After applying ct-UAEs to predict formation energy in hybrid perovskites database, we realized an improvement in accuracy, with a 34% boost in MEGNET and 16% in CGCNN, showcasing their potential as atomic ﬁngerprints to address the data scarcity challenges.

stages.stage_name_raw: Screen optimal clustering configuration for interpretability
stages.stage_goal: Determine the optimal number of clusters for interpreting ct-UAEs via clustering analysis.
stage_input: clustering algorithms (UMAP, K-means, t-SNE, community detection)

evidence.text: To determine the best number of clusters for atoms, the elbow plots56 and siltouette coefﬁcient graphs56 are needed, with quantitative analysis shown in Fig. 3b, c. Both elbow plot and silhouette coefﬁcient graph demonstrate that 3 or 4 clusters’ solution is the best choice for the classiﬁcation of atoms.

Based on the clustering results, most of the elements in the periodic table can be categorized, as shown in Fig. 3a. This example divides all elements into 3 classes, called as Class A (the green cluster), Class B (the yellow cluster), and Class C (the blue cluster).

stages.stage_name_raw: Validate ct-UAE physical interpretability via reverse prediction
stages.stage_goal: Validate that ct-UAEs encode meaningful physical/chemical atomic properties by training a CatBoost model to predict elemental properties from embeddings.
stage_input: elemental properties (atomic radius, boiling temperature, etc.)
stage_output: R2 scores for reverse prediction (e.g., >0.78 for all properties)

evidence.text: To further investigate the intrinsic information of the embeddings, we conduct reverse training experiments, which involves taking a series of important elemental properties, including atomic radius, boiling temperature, melting temperature, electrical conductivity, ﬁrst ionization energy as training targets to train a Catboost model66. 80% of atomic embeddings are selected randomly as training data, while the rest serves as validation to calculate R2 (coefﬁcient of determination). The R2 for the model in predicting each property is calculated, with the best results listed in Table 4, which reveals that, the Catboost model exhibits high values of R2 larger than 0.78.
